Currently
column2: the dynptr function is not checking the variable offset part

column1: of PTR_TO_STACK that it needs to check. The fixed offset is considered
when computing the stack pointer index
column2: but if the variable offset was

column1: not a constant (such that it could not be accumulated in reg->off)
will end up a discrepency where runtime pointer does not point to the
actual stack slot we mark as STACK_DYNPTR.
It is impossible to precisely track dynptr state when variable offset is
not constant
simply reject the case where reg->var_off is not constant. Then
consider both reg->off and reg->var_off.value when computing the stack
pointer index.
A new helper dynptr_get_spi is introduced to hide over these details
since the dynptr needs to be located in multiple places outside the
process_dynptr_func checks
column2: hence once we know it's a PTR_TO_STACK

column1: need to enforce these checks in all places.
Note that it is disallowed for unprivileged users to have a non-constant
var_off
column2: so this problem should only be possible to trigger from

column1: programs having CAP_PERFMON. However
Without the fix
column2: it is possible to replace the contents of the dynptr

column1: arbitrarily by making verifier mark different stack slots than actual
location and then doing writes to the actual stack address of dynptr at
runtime.
